suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-15 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. A prospective birth cohort followed to age 32 found generalized anxiety disorder and major depressive disorder strongly comorbid with roughly symmetric onset ordering, so the approved relationship is limited to cumulative/sequential comorbidity and does not assert that generalized anxiety disorder precedes or causes depression. Require independently established generalized anxiety disorder and separately established major depressive disorder. The cited prospective birth cohort found cumulative and roughly symmetric sequential comorbidity, with depression onset first, anxiety onset first, and concurrent onset each occurring in about one third of comorbid cases; do not treat either disorder as reliably primary in onset order. Preserve other psychiatric illness, substance use, medical illness, medications, psychosocial stressors, and shared vulnerability as competing explanations. Treat this only as population-level comorbidity association, not proof that generalized anxiety disorder caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
